messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: routing-fallback-anomaly detected across regions us-east <-> us-west <-> eu — escalated to P1, paging oncall
maria: i'm on it. seeing spike in 503s and tail latency from the gateway metrics. graphs: https://grafana.internal/redwood/routing?panel=fallthrough
alex: I can see healthchecks flipping for runtime-probe in us-west and eu, then clients getting routed back to us-east and failing there. looks like a small ping timeout is cascading.
samir: logs show repeated health-check toggles every ~30s for the probe agent group. Cursor: probe-agent-47 shows: `503 ping timeout -> healthy` then `unhealthy -> 504` in a loop.
kai: any recent routing policy changes? I pushed a fallback tweak yesterday to prefer model-variant v2 in eu. could that be involved?
maria: possibly. the fallback policy now maps model variants across regions when local capacity is low. if health flags are noisy, the policy might be bouncing requests between region+variant pairs.
jamie: customer support reporting errors for interactive endpoints in us-east and eu. tickets coming in with request ids. severity seems widespread for a handful of high-volume orgs.
nora: paging rota: maria is primary, alex backup. samir and kai on rotation. let's coordinate mitigation steps.
maria: initial mitigation: disable cross-region fallback routing to stop the hop chain. executing now: `redwoodctl routing update --id fallback-global --enabled false` — running.
incident-bot: command accepted. fallback-global disabled (api response 200).
alex: confirm deploy: routes now only prefer local region and will return 429 if capacity exceeded instead of failing over. that'll increase local throttles but avoid loop.
samir: good. i'll increase probe debounce window to reduce flip rate: patching probe-config: `health.check.retry_window: 120s` -> applying to us-west+eu.
kai: also recommending raising KV cache TTL for routing decisions to give a cooldown: `routing.cache.ttl: 300s` while we investigate.
maria: applying both changes.

# quick commands run
```
redwoodctl config set probe-agent --region us-west --key health.check.retry_window --value 120s
redwoodctl config set routing --key routing.cache.ttl --value 300s
```

alex: after disabling fallback and applying debounces, 503 rate dropped by ~70% in us-east within 60s. latency tail improving. grafana panels look cleaner.
jamie: support: please prepare a short customer-facing note. list affected endpoints and that we're throttling rather than failing over to prevent cross-region impact.

maria: drafting: "We've applied a temporary mitigation to routing policies to prevent cross-region request oscillation. Some requests may receive transient rate-limit responses while we stabilize. We're continuing remediation and will follow up with timeline." anyone want to change wording?
jamie: fine. add: "no data loss; requests may be retried." also include contact for escalation.
nora: we should also check model-variant mismatch. kai, can you confirm the variant mapping matrix? maybe v2 in eu is not binary-compatible with v1 in us-east and causes failure mode.
kai: checking. the mapping uses a compatibility label, but we discovered yesterday that a small serialization change in v2 causes runtime deserial to return 500s for certain tokenization edge cases. fallback was moving traffic to v2 in eu when us-east was flapping -> causing more errors -> more fallback.
samir: ok that's a root cause lead: variant incompatibility + aggressive fallback = oscillation.

maria: proposed next steps:
- keep cross-region fallback disabled (short-term)
- revert the variant mapping that routes to v2 across regions
- run a targeted canary test for v2 compatibility in eu only with synthetic load
- add adaptive cooldown to fallback policy before re-enabling

alex: I'll revert the variant mapping now: `redwoodctl models mapping set --policy-id cross-region-variant --map \"us-east:v1,us-west:v1,eu:v1\"`
incident-bot: Operation queued, awaiting approval.
maria: approving.
incident-bot: Operation applied (200). variant cross-region map set to prefer v1 everywhere.
kai: starting canary harness in eu with 1% traffic and focused prompt set. logs go to /logs/variant-canary/eu/2801128999
samir: creating follow-up incident ticket to track root cause and long-term fix: better preflight checks for variant compatibility and safer fallback cooldowns. I'll assign to eng-runtime and eng-sre.

jamie: is there any customer data impact? support says no persisted data lost, just request errors and retries.
maria: confirmed. no data corruption. CBs retried successfully after we disabled fallback. marking customer-impact: degraded UX for some high-load customers, no data loss.
nora: timeline update for postmortem: start time = 2801128999, mitigation in place = 2801129155, variant revert = 2801129250, probe debounce applied = 2801129300. we'll collect traces for the window.

alex: final checklist before unpaging: monitoring alert will be silenced for routing-fallback-anomaly for 2 hours while we verify.
incident-bot: alert muted for 2h by maria.
maria: handing off to samir for longer-term follow-up. samir, take over oncall progress.
samir: taking over. will coordinate postmortem and remediation. thanks team :thumbsup:
jamie: i'll send a customer update and tag affected customers. closing P1 after postmortem ticket created.

maria: unassigning oncall. if anything flips back, re-page immediately.
nora: thanks everyone. good coordination."
